senses: Concerned with the interests of others more than one's own; community-minded.

Of spatial representations: linked to a reference frame based on the external environment and independent of one's current location in it (for example, giving a direction as "north" as opposed to "right").
Of a tourist: tending to be adventurous and preferring novel and unfamiliar experiences.
ety: The adjective is derived from allo- (prefix meaning ‘different; other’) + -centric (suffix meaning ‘having a specified object at the centre, or as the focus of attention’). Sense 3 (‘of a tourist: tending to be adventurous’) was coined by the American travel researcher Stanley C. Plog in a paper presented to the Southern California Chapter of the Travel Research Association on 10 October 1972, which was later published in February 1974. The noun is probably derived from the adjective.

senses: The freehanded art of decorating wood, leather or other materials with burn marks (resulting in surface burned designs) from the controlled application of a heated object or tool such as a poker.
A decoration or design so produced.
A manufacturer of weapons, especially of guns.
A military specialist in charge of the upkeep of small arms etc.
Someone who makes or repairs armor.
ety: From Middle English armurer, from Old French armurier. By surface analysis, armor + -er.

senses: A person who attends visitors in a religious institution.
A member of any of several religious orders that cared for the sick in hospitals.
ety: From Middle English hospiteler, from Middle French hospitalier; equivalent to hospital + -er. Piecewise doublet of hosteller.

senses: A concept of virtue and honor within a family, typically relating to chastity of female family members.
A cromlech, a stone circle, a lithic burial structure in the Sinai connected to various superstitions.
ety: From Arabic نَامُوس (nāmūs). Doublet of nome and nomos.

senses: Having two levels.
examples: We developed a bilevel approach to the problem.

senses: A person who broils, someone who cooks by broiling.
A device used to broil food; part of an oven or a small stove; known as a grill in British English.
A chicken raised for meat.
Specifically, a young chicken 6 to 10 weeks old, as contrasted with a roaster.
ety: From broil + -er (agent noun suffix) or, for the chickens, + -er (patient suffix).

senses: Not refundable; not able to be refunded.
A female member of the bourgeoisie; a wealthy woman
examples: She is a right-wing bourgeoise; he is on the left.

senses: A closely-cropped military-style haircut.
Shaped like a boat's keel.
ety: Borrowed from Latin carīnātus, from carīna (“keel”) + -ātus, see -ate (adjective-forming suffix). The noun comes from a substantivization of the adjective, see -ate (noun-forming suffix).

senses: Any sexual act deemed against nature, such as homosexuality, bestiality or necrophilia.
A film archive with small cinemas, screening classic and art-house films.
The state of being obsolete—no longer in use; gone into disuse; disused or neglected.
The process of becoming obsolete, outmoded or out of date.
ety: From Latin obsolēscēns (present participle of obsolēscere).

senses: Ribbons of pasta, cut from a sheet, not as wide as tagliatelle.
ety: Borrowed from Italian linguine (literally “little tongues”), from lingua (“tongue”).

senses: An ideology based on the belief that people, goods and information ought to be able to cross national borders unfettered.
A socio-economic system dedicated to free trade and free access to markets.
Someone who participates in something for a certain number of weeks.
examples: Most holidaymakers are two-weekers, but a few are three-weekers.

senses: A yaku (scoring condition) and 1000-point bet made by declaring the hand to be ready, waiting for one more tile to win.
A call for such a bet.
Being one symbol away from getting a jackpot, usually triggering an animation before the final symbol is revealed.
ety: From Japanese 立直 (rīchi), from Chinese 立直 (lìzhí).

senses: An aristocrat.
examples: This is a beautiful world of enlightened aristos, the kind of people who know not only wine but Italian art and, to a great extent, themselves.

senses: A physical location where work is done, especially construction work.
Having the characteristics of pulp.
Having the characteristics of pulp fiction; thus, having a garish focus on sex and violence.
examples: In a sly bit of casting, Tony Goldwyn — a star of the pulpy TV series “Scandal” — shows up as one of the leaders of the Christmas Adventurers Club..

senses: A savoury fishcake delicacy from Indonesia (Palembang), made of fish, egg, and tapioca usually served with the traditional spice-based broth and sometimes also served with noodles.
ety: Learned borrowing from Indonesian pempek, derived from Musi pempek.

senses: Prolixity; diffuse discourse.
The act of dilating; expansion; an enlarging on all sides; the state of being dilated
A dilation or enlargement of a canal or other organ.
ety: From Old French dilatation, from Late Latin dīlātātio, early 15th c.

senses: Characteristic of a doof; stupid
Destitute of any vestige of organic life, or at least of animal life.
Before the existence of animal life.
Able to be renewed or replenished.
examples: Time is the most perishable good in the world, and it is not replenishable.

senses: The Japanese custom of enjoying the beauty of flowers, usually cherry blossoms or plum blossoms, also known as "flower viewing".
A palm (Borassus flabellifer) with straight black upright trunk and palmate leaves, whose wood, fruit, and roots can be used for many purposes.
ety: From Portuguese palmeira (“palm tree”), from palma (“palm, palm tree”) + -eria (“-tree: forming tree names”), from Old Galician-Portuguese -eira (“-plant: forming plant names from their fruit”), from Latin -āria (“-ary: forming feminine nouns including plant names”).

senses: A video and/or audio broadcast produced by fans of a work or subject.
One who darts, or who throws darts; that which darts.
Any member of the family Anhingidae, waterbirds with long necks.
A game of darts that is won with the specified number of darts thrown.
examples: With a scoring target of 501, a nine-darter is a perfect game.

senses: A stag in its second year, before its horns have started branching.
ety: Borrowed from Middle French brocart, broquart.

senses: Having oars.
Someone who munches.
The phase of a perfume where the top note gives way to the base note.
The physiologically mature phase in the ripening of a crop, where the fruit attains the desired trait of desiccation, suiting it for harvest and storage (e.g. maize, soybean).
A period where the habitat of a hydrophile organism is desiccated.
ety: From dry + down and deverbal from dry down.

senses: A resident of a nursing home who has limited means and whose accommodation is consequently partly paid for by the government.
examples: Every weekend and after work she'd done the rounds of the nursing homes. All are bound by law to take a percentage of 'concessionals'. But the waiting lists! On one he's placed at seventy-five.

senses: A tall chest of drawers, or combination of chest on chest, or chest with a small wardrobe on top. Usually with low bracket feet but always resulting in a tall piece of furniture.
A tall beer can, either 16 or 24 ounces (473 or 710ml).
A kind of long-stemmed wineglass or cup.
A long sheet-metal pipe for a chimney top.
ety: By surface analysis, tall + boy, but the furniture sense may have been originally modeled after lowboy, related to French bois (“wood”).
examples: In her post, which was less than a minute long, she said that the company had sent her a tallboy can of Bud Light with her face on it. An image of the can was edited into the video.

senses: A person who has malaria.
The state or quality of being factual.
That which is factual.
Marked by craters.
examples: The planet had a cratered surface.

The Mariner photos showed large areas of the red planet to have a much-cratered surface strikingly like that of the moon. Now the computers have clarified some previously undecipherable closeups taken by Mariner 6.

senses: A traditional steamed dumpling made from rice flour and lentil filling, popular in Northern India.
